Minor release: `@claude-flow/cli`, `claude-flow`, `ruflo` 3.67.0, with standalone `@claude-flow/aidefence` 3.1.0 and `@claude-flow/memory` 3.2.1. It rides on the ecosystem releases agentdb 3.0.0, agentic-flow 3.0.0 and npm `aidefence` 3.0.1 (ADR-513 to ADR-517).

### Security
- **Prompt-injection detection runs the AIMDS pattern packs** (`@claude-flow/aidefence` 3.1.0, ADR-517). Six packs and 53 patterns now run alongside the built-in regexes, covering tool-invocation, exfiltration-URL, encoded, markup-carrier, multilingual and Slack-forgery injections. On the AIMDS corpus, detection goes from 8/55 to 55/55, with the same 2 known false positives. Turn the packs off with `createAIDefence({ packs: false })`. A quadratic leet normaliser found while vendoring them is fixed here and upstream (npm `aidefence` 3.0.1).
- **aidefence restored to source** (3.0.4 → 3.1.0, ADR-516). npm `latest` 3.0.3 carried ADR-118 detection that was never committed; it is ported back alongside main's #3177 ReDoS bounds. The CLI had pinned 3.0.2, so ruflo users get both for the first time.
- **A fresh install's dependency tree converges** (ADR-513). agentdb 3.0.0 is stable, so the optional peer ranges that excluded `3.0.0-alpha.20` now match it. One AgentDB copy is installed instead of three, and agentic-flow 3.0.0 replaces the March 3.0.0-alpha.2, which pulled `protobufjs@6` (critical).
  - Measured on a fresh install: `npm audit --omit=dev` went from 70 advisories (1 critical, 17 high) on 3.66.1 to 11 (0 critical) with these packages. The remaining high advisory is zod 3.
- **agentic-flow 3.0.0 defaults** (ADR-515, agentic-flow ADR-079): proxies bind loopback with a per-run token, agents no longer bypass permissions, and a cloned repo's `.env` or router config can no longer redirect API keys. The release also fixes path traversal in its agent tools and code execution through `statusline.sh`.
- **agentdb 3.0.0** (ADR-514): `agentdb_init` no longer deletes arbitrary files, filter-key SQL inj

Security patch: `@claude-flow/cli`, `claude-flow`, `ruflo` 3.66.2, with the bundled `@claude-flow/mcp` 3.1.5 and `@claude-flow/security` 3.0.6 (also published standalone).

### Security
- **Bearer tokens are parsed in linear time** (`@claude-flow/mcp`). The HTTP and WebSocket transports matched `Authorization` with `/^Bearer\s+(.+)$/i`. That pattern backtracks quadratically on a long run of whitespace followed by a line break (CodeQL js/polynomial-redos). Node's HTTP parser already rejects line breaks in header values, so this is hardening rather than a reachable denial of service. Both transports now use a prefix compare and `trimStart`, and refuse headers over 8 KB.
- **Verification codes are uniform** (`@claude-flow/security`). `TokenGenerator.generateVerificationCode()` used `byte % 10`, so digits 0-5 came up 26/256 of the time and 6-9 only 25/256. Each digit now comes from `crypto.randomInt(10)`.
- **`sanitizeString` cannot be tricked into rebuilding a protocol** (`@claude-flow/security`). One pass turned `javajavascript:script:` into `javascript:`. It now strips `javascript:`, `vbscript:` and `data:` until none remain.
- `terminal_create` session ids come from `crypto.randomBytes` rather than `Math.random`.


PR: #4624. Follow-up for the dependency tree: #4625.
name: v3.66.2 — security hardening: bearer parsing, verification codes, protocol stripping

## ✨ Highlights

- **👥 Separate sessions in one browser** — work with multiple accounts without sharing their cookies or storage. `browser_tabs` with `action: "new"` now accepts `isolatedContext: "<name>"`: tabs with the same name share a context, while different names stay isolated. Omit it or use `"default"` for the default context. Cookie and storage tools operate on the current tab's context. ([microsoft/playwright#43087](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/pull/43087))
- **🙈 Redact runtime values in URLs** ([#1791](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright-mcp/issues/1791)) — session and grant values minted at runtime cannot be listed in a secrets file ahead of time. `--redact-url-params=access_token,code` (config `redactUrlParams`, env `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_REDACT_URL_PARAMS`) replaces the named query and fragment parameter values with `<redacted>` in tool responses. Like `secrets`, this is a convenience, not a security feature. The extension also removes its connection token from the connect page URL after reading it. ([microsoft/playwright#43258](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/pull/43258))
- **🔎 Bound find results** ([microsoft/playwright#42077](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/42077)) — common search terms no longer have to fill the response with every match. `browser_find` accepts a positive integer `maxResults`, returns the first matching items with their context, and reports the total match count. Omit it to keep returning all matches; ancestor paths are unchanged. ([microsoft/playwright#42947](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/pull/42947))
- **🌐 Inspect requests across navigations** ([microsoft/playwright-cli#479](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright-cli/issues/479)) — requests from the previous page are no longer lost as soon as a flow navigates. `browser_network_requests` accepts `all: true` to include retained history, keeping up to 200 requests from earlier navigations. Request indexes stay stable across navigations

Patch release: `@claude-flow/cli`, `claude-flow`, `ruflo` 3.66.1, plus standalone `@claude-flow/memory` 3.2.0 and `@claude-flow/plugin-agent-federation` 1.0.4.

### Security
- **Federation trust thresholds are now enforced** (#4618, #4619). `SecurityPolicy.minTrustLevelForWrite`, `minTrustLevelForMemory` and `minTrustLevelForSpawn` were declared and accepted as overrides but never checked.
  - Before: `memory-query` and `memory-response` passed at `ATTESTED`, below the default policy's own `TRUSTED` minimum.
  - Now: `PolicyEngine.evaluateMessage()` checks the configured minimum for write, memory and spawn messages. The check adds to the built-in capability gates; a looser policy cannot bypass them.

### Fixed
- **A memory store locked by another process now says so** (#4622). Separate stdio MCP servers opening one store contend for its native vector store.
  - Before: AgentDB fell back to a backend that rejected the locked file as the wrong format, and only that error was reported. The registry was still treated as available, and memory operations then failed with an unrelated sql.js WAL refusal.
  - Now: `ControllerRegistry.getAgentDBInitError()` (`@claude-flow/memory` 3.2.0) keeps the first backend's failure, such as `Database already open. Cannot acquire lock`. It names the fix: run one owner with `ruflo mcp start --transport http` and point every client at it. The CLI bridge records that reason and adds it to the fallback's refusal. `isBridgeAvailable()` returns false when AgentDB did not open.
  - `memory_list` reports a failed query as `success: false` with its error, not as an empty inventory.
name: v3.66.1 — federation trust thresholds enforced; locked memory stores say so

Agent Skills 0.6.15 stops the security skill's staged-secret check from printing the secret it finds, fixes two simplify-ignore bugs that could corrupt protected code, and makes the constraints skill's security and accessibility gates actually fail CI.

## Security

- **The staged-secret check no longer echoes credentials** (#718, @santhiprakash, reported by @xmxxc in #717). The old `git diff --cached | grep` printed every matching line, so a staged key landed in the terminal and in any agent's transcript. It also read as clean when git failed. The check is now `git diff --cached -i -G'…' --name-only`: it prints only file names, and a git failure exits non-zero by itself. Fixed in all three places it was documented.

## Hooks

- **simplify-ignore restores re-indented placeholders cleanly** (#766, @Quinnod345, #765). If `/code-simplify` un-indented a placeholder or edited its reason, Stop wrote back a broken comment around the block, a syntax error in any `/* */` language. Blocks marked with `-- simplify-ignore-start` (SQL, Lua, Haskell) no longer warn that they were deleted, and a missing lock directory no longer stops Stop before every file is restored.

## Skills

- **Quality gates that fail when they should** (#694, @mavericksea-ai, #693). Semgrep and axe exit 0 even with blocking findings, so the constraints skill's examples could pass CI while breaking the written bar. Security patch: `@claude-flow/cli`, `claude-flow`, `ruflo` 3.65.1. Contains 3.65.0 plus this one fix (#4605).

### Security
- **`http_fetch` SSRF via DNS** (CWE-918, CWE-350).
  - Before: the MCP tool refused loopback, RFC-1918 and link-local hosts only by the URL's hostname text, then let `fetch()` resolve the name itself. A hostname that resolves, or rebinds, to `127.0.0.1`, a private address or `169.254.169.254` reached it without `CLAUDE_FLOW_HTTP_FETCH_ALLOW_PRIVATE`.
  - Now: every connection resolves through a lookup hook. The hook refuses the host if any resolved address is private, and the socket connects only to addresses it checked. Every redirect hop is checked the same way.
  - The address check also covers `::`, IPv4-compatible and NAT64/6to4 IPv6 forms, `fe80::/10`, `fec0::/10`, `ff00::/8`, IPv4 multicast/reserved, `198.18.0.0/15` and `*.localhost`.


Fix PR: #4605. Install: `npx ruflo@3.65.1` (all of `latest`, `alpha`, `v3alpha` point here).

Eigent v1.0.7 lets you work with several Sessions at once, side by side or in their own windows, adds a Session menu and message actions, and makes Automations start reliably, once, and on your local time.

This update also fixes a long list of bugs found in testing and reported by the community, from approvals and quitting to sign-in after an update.

### Highlights

- **Sessions side by side** — Show up to three Sessions next to each other in a Space, or open a Session in its own window or browser tab. Background work such as scheduled Automations starts from only one window, so nothing runs twice.
- **Session menu** — Click the Session title to pin, rename, end or delete it, or turn the Session into a skill or an Automation.
- **Message actions** — Copy a message, edit and resend it, or expand a long one. A divider shows when the model changes between tasks.
- **Space overview** — See an overview of the Space in a panel beside the Workspace composer.
- **Redesigned Dispatch page** — The Remote Control page has a new layout.
- **BytePlus ModelArk sub-agents** — Add BytePlus ModelArk managed agents as a remote sub-agent provider from a redesigned Settings → Sub-agents page.
- **Out of credits, not out of options** — When your Eigent credits run out, upgrade your plan or switch to your own API key straight from the notice.

### Automations

- Run now starts the Automation right away, and runs the app never received are recovered.
- Automations are listed for the whole Space, and their schedules stay in your local time.
- An Automation runs only once when you open its Session afterwards.

### Approvals, questions and tasks

- Approvals and questions appear above the message box and name the file or command they are for.
- A question still waiting after a reload can be answered, and the agent's question and your answer stay in the chat.
- Memory changes ask for confirmation and show their details.
- Follow-up messages wait in the queue until a failed task is resolved.

# ESP32 firmware v0.8.17 — experimental C5 support

Adds an experimental ESP32-C5 headless firmware bundle alongside S3/C6, guarded C5 installation, and user/build guides. C5's bootloader is at 0x2000; select the matching bundle and verify both archive and image checksums.

## Fixed
- Prevents legacy mmWave GPIO17/18 probing from rerouting the C5 flash/PSRAM bus. Unconfigured C5 sensor probes are skipped; explicit pins are checked against memory and console assignments.
- Flash qualification and the public SDK monitor reject watchdog/flash-busy evidence even if initial CSI callbacks appear.
- C5 writes require production-chip identity, sufficient flash and esptool >=5.3.
- Updates libz-sys for RUSTSEC-2026-0418; bounds harness test concurrency for Windows helper startup.

## Real hardware evidence and limits

**MEASURED (bounded real hardware; reproducer in the linked record):** Production ESP32-C5HR8 revision 1.2 with 8 MB flash was backed up, installed and provisioned. Corrected firmware 0.8.17 booted and streamed real CSI without captured watchdog/flash-busy errors in bounded captures. The production SDK receiver decoded all 971 packets in its recorded sample with no malformed or unknown packets.

Cadence was AP-dependent: recorded raw CSI samples were roughly 12?29 packets/s. Bounded extra traffic did not produce a consistent improvement. This setup did not consistently meet the 20 packets/s acceptance target. C5 remains experimental; this is not a sensing-accuracy, comparative speedup or long-run reliability qualification.

Profile: 2.4 GHz, 240 MHz CPU, 8 Hz edge DSP, 4 MB OTA layout, UART console. Display, WASM and PSRAM are disabled. 5 GHz is not qualified. Exact board form factor remains operator-unconfirmed; the generic profile has no LED or default sensor pin assignment.

## My Work: one store for the viewer's state (#5187)

My Work used to keep its state in three places: a hand-rolled module store, component state in `App`, and React contexts. It now runs on one Zustand store split into four slices: work, view, rules and focus.

**What you'll notice**
- **Reload and Back/Forward work.** The page, focus area and open request drawer are in the URL (`?view=`, `?focus=`, `?request=`).
- **Your list view, filter and sort are remembered** between visits. The theme still follows your system or `?theme=`. If browser storage is blocked, preferences last for the current visit only.
- **Live updates are steadier.** A stopped source can't publish. An older read never overwrites a newer live model. When a live update overtakes a save, you see the current model and your save is kept. Heartbeats re-render only the status indicators.
- **The drawer follows its request** by id and closes when the request leaves the feed. If the first read fails, you get a Retry button. A selected Closed filter stays visible even when nothing matches.
- **My Rules:** one save at a time, with controls disabled while a save runs. Each Approve/Reject receipt is tied to the version the worker saved, and Undo is refused once the rule has changed since.
- **My Focus:** all screens share one save history.

**Worker**
- Rule saves return `savedRuleId`.
- "Load in Claude Code" publishes the change to other open tabs.
- The feed signature includes `rulesFile`.

Agent Skills 0.6.14 is mostly about code samples. More than twenty snippets across the skills either failed as written or taught the wrong thing, and they're fixed. It also closes two supply-chain and injection risks in the samples, stops Claude Code from starting `/ship` or `/build` on its own, and brings the root manifest in line with Agent Plugins 1.0.0.

## Security fixes in the samples

- **The Lighthouse CI example ran the unscoped `lhci` package** (#721), which isn't Lighthouse CI. It now invokes `@lhci/cli`.
- **The rollback workflow passed its input straight into `run:`** (#691), a script injection in any repo that copied it. It goes through `env` now.
- The constraints skill scans the working tree for secrets, not only commits (#729), and the hardening reference returns 404 before an ownership check reads a missing task (#726).

## Samples that now work as written

- **Accessibility:** labels are tied to their controls (#719), the loading region has a role so its label is exposed (#725), and the axe example runs the CLI that actually ships a binary (#720).
- **Testing and debugging:** the Playwright example finds list items by their text (#688), the Jest example isolates a file in a way Jest 30 still accepts (#712), and the coverage setup installs Vitest's coverage provider, without which CI fails (#713).
- **Frontend:** the task list passes its toggle and delete handlers down (#706), and the empty state declares its action prop (#692).

## Faster diff view and editor, more languages, and better remote files 🌍

This release adds four interface languages, makes switching workspaces faster by preparing the one you’re about to open, and lets files on SSH hosts and paired servers play, save and open like local ones. It also brings smoother chat streaming, a faster prompt in new Windows terminals, steadier WSL terminals, and many fixes for dictation on the phone.

## The short version

- **Four new languages:** German, Russian, Turkish and Traditional Chinese join the language picker, and many more dialogs, menus and shortcuts are translated. German is machine-translated, and reviews from native speakers are welcome.
- **Faster workspace switching:** Hovering a workspace in the sidebar gets it ready, the workspaces next to the current one stay warm, and the switch itself does less work. Dragging a row never switches.
- **Remote files that work like local ones:** Play audio and video from SSH hosts and paired servers, save remote text files up to 50 MB, open folders too big for one reply as you scroll, and never open a remote binary as text.
- **Smoother chats:** Long replies stream with less stutter, @file suggestions keep up in large repositories, and multi-agent Codex chats no longer grow the local chat history to gigabytes. Claude chats can rewind to before your first message.
- **Steadier terminals:** New Windows terminals show their prompt right away instead of after about 3 seconds, closing or resizing a terminal no longer freezes the others on macOS and Linux, and WSL terminals keep their session and folder when their distro stops.
- **Browser:** Clear Google cookies from a profile when Google sign-in is stuck on an old account, import cookies from Vivaldi, and Orca no longer quits at startup on Windows and Linux when an extension’s helper window closes.
- **Fixes from the community:** Kimi K3 for commit messages, Devin Desktop in Open In, highlighting for Glimmer, CUDA, Groovy and shebang scripts

## English

### Summary

This stable release brings interactive HTML inside Markdown results to Web, Desktop and the browser extension, with a redesigned output pipeline for concurrent generation and large responses. It also improves backup integrity, adds import codes for selected cloud backups, preserves model selections and saved parameters, and refines image-editing and structured-input templates.

### Highlights

- **Interactive output in place:** use Preview or Source to inspect results. Explicit HTML code blocks and supported HTML content render as isolated web pages alongside the surrounding Markdown. Multiple blocks can remain interactive at the same time.

- Use the shared Preview/Source output interface, inline HTML previews and backup import-code flow.

#### Web

- Render multiple HTML examples directly in Markdown results. Switching one result to Source leaves other results' previews intact.

## My Work: focus areas, and requests that file themselves

### Focus areas are the top level of My Work (#5131)
- **MY FOCUS rail.** Your focus areas are listed in priority order, with a needs-you count on each. Every request sits in exactly one area, or in **Other**. On phones the areas appear as a chip row.
- **Area header.** Each area page shows its goal sentence, combined progress, your own quotes, the asks you haven't started yet, and a link to Past focus. The My Goals page is retired; its content now lives here.
- **Suggested.** New areas appear here by themselves. You can Keep, Rename, Merge or Dismiss each one, with Undo. Your decisions sync across computers and a refresh never overrides them.
- **Owner-goals sorts what it mines.** It applies three tests in order, so each statement becomes exactly one focus area, ask or rule. Priorities and open asks no longer duplicate each other.
- **The Focus step replaces Align in the automatic refresh.** It places every request, and it proposes new areas from Other or from a request that holds several separate asks.
- **Request cards.** Every card shows its area, and request detail has **Move to…**. "What came out of it" is now called **Deliverables**.

### The judge files new conversations under their request (#5110)

Build a `Skill` in Python or load one from a folder or package, publish it through `SkillCatalogProvider`, and let clients discover its metadata or download and export its files. Ask an agent for a deck, a report, an HTML page or any other file, and it is one click away on the front of the request's card in My Work, under **Deliverables**.

The same kind of built-in engine that ships with [AnythingLLM Desktop](https://docs.anythingllm.com/setup/llm-configuration/local/built-in) can now run **inside the container**: [Lemonade](https://lemonade-server.ai), the fully [open-source](https://github.com/lemonade-sdk/lemonade) local inference server from AMD, running your models with [llama.cpp](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp). You no longer need to run Ollama, LM Studio or any other inference server next to AnythingLLM. Pass your GPU into the container and the engine is accelerated on whatever hardware you have. It picks the fastest backend automatically: CUDA for NVIDIA GPUs, Vulkan for AMD and Intel GPUs, or the CPU. It runs on both `amd64` and `arm64` hosts. When it's turned on, **Built-in** becomes the default LLM provider during onboarding, with three models recommended for your hardware. You can download any model from the model table or pull any GGUF model from Hugging Face. It works everywhere a provider can be used: the system LLM, workspace and agent LLMs, the chat window model picker, and [Model Router](https://docs.anythingllm.com/model-router/setup). > [!TIP] > **The built-in LLM is off by default.** Turn it on by starting the container with `-e ENABLE_BUILT_IN_LLM=true`, and add `--gpus all` (or pass in your AMD or Intel GPU devices) for GPU acceleration. See [Built-in LLM for Docker](https://docs.anythingllm.com/installation-docker/built-in-llm) for the full setup for each kind of hardware. ### Color palettes Color palettes are straightforward thematic tinting you can apply to the entire UI.
